Adaptive loss definitions

Functional repulsion

z_h=(\mu_h(s_b))_{b=1}^{P}

Weight repulsion

z_h=\operatorname{vec}(\theta_h)

FoRDE

g_h=(\partial\mu_h(s_b)/\partial s_b)_{b=1}^{P},\qquad z_h=g_h/\sqrt{\|g_h\|^2+\varepsilon_g}
C(\Theta)=\frac{1}{H(H-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|z_i-z_j\|^2}{h_0}\right)
h_0=\max\{\operatorname{median}_{i<j}\|z_i^{(0)}-z_j^{(0)}\|^2,\varepsilon_h\},\qquad c=rC(\Theta_0)
\min_\Theta L_{\mathrm{fit}}(\Theta)\quad\mathrm{subject\ to}\quad C(\Theta)\le c
\mathcal L(\Theta,\lambda)=L_{\mathrm{fit}}(\Theta)+\lambda(C(\Theta)-c)
\lambda_{t+1}=\max\{0,\lambda_t+\eta_\lambda[C(\Theta_{t+1})-c]\}
L_{\mathrm{fit}}=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\frac{1}{2B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\left[\log(2\pi v_h(x_{hb}))+(y_{hb}-\mu_h(x_{hb}))^2/v_h(x_{hb})\right]

H: network count; P: fixed reference count; μ and v: predicted mean and variance; θ: trainable parameters; r: target ratio (default 0.8); ηλ: multiplier step size (default 0.1); λ₀ = 0; εh = 10⁻⁶; εg = 10⁻⁸. Both sides of every pair receive gradients. The bandwidth, reference inputs, and target remain fixed.

Training uses all training inputs. Random uses an equally sized fixed uniform domain set excluding training inputs. Combined uses their union. Weight repulsion is input-independent. Stage two retains the existing BDKN Bayesian marginal-NLL objective on frozen trained features.

Stage-one curves average pre-update minibatch losses. Similarity and violation curves use the full reference set after each epoch; λ after the update is shown separately. The Lagrangian includes −λc and can be negative.

This is a proposed constrained-diversity extension, distinct from the saved KDE objectives. Target ratio, bandwidth rule, and step sizes are experimental choices. Nonconvex training has no asserted global-convergence or uncertainty-calibration guarantee.

References: Boyd–Vandenberghe, Chapter 5; Haarnoja et al., Section 5; Trinh et al., FoRDE.
